title: Curry for shogi
setting: A weekday evening. Kenta doesn't pick up, so Satou-san, the elderly neighbour, leaves him a voicemail. The day before, Kenta had brought him some homemade curry.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.ja: もしもし、ケンタくん？佐藤です。
lines.kana: もしもし、けんたくん？さとうです。

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kinou wa, oishii karee o arigatou gozaimashita. onaka ippai ni narimashita.
lines.ja: 昨日は、おいしいカレーをありがとうございました。お腹いっぱいになりました。
lines.kana: きのうは、おいしいかれーをありがとうございました。おなかいっぱいになりました。
lines.english: Thank you for the delicious curry yesterday. I ate until I was full.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hontou ni ki ni itte, kesa mo tabemashita yo.
lines.ja: 本当に気に入って、今朝も食べましたよ。
lines.kana: ほんとうにきにいって、けさもたべましたよ。
lines.english: I loved it so much, I had some again this morning.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hitotsu ki ni natta n desu ga, ano karee, nani ga haitte ita n desu ka?
lines.ja: 一つ気になったんですが、あのカレー、何が入っていたんですか？
lines.kana: ひとつきになったんですが、あのかれー、なにがはいっていたんですか？
lines.english: One thing made me curious, though. What was in that curry?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: totemo ki ni itta node, jibun de mo tsukutte mitai n desu.
lines.ja: とても気に入ったので、自分でも作ってみたいんです。
lines.kana: とてもきにいったので、じぶんでもつくってみたいんです。
lines.english: I liked it so much that I'd like to try making it myself.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: zutto, ryouri ni kyoumi ga atta n desu. demo, gohan o tsukuru no wa, jishin ga nakute ne.
lines.ja: ずっと、料理に興味があったんです。でも、ご飯を作るのは、自信がなくてね。
lines.kana: ずっと、りょうりにきょうみがあったんです。でも、ごはんをつくるのは、じしんがなくてね。
lines.english: I've always been interested in cooking. But I've never felt confident making meals, you see.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kenta-kun, karee no tsukurikata, oshiete moraemasen ka?
lines.ja: ケンタくん、カレーの作り方、教えてもらえませんか？
lines.kana: けんたくん、かれーのつくりかた、おしえてもらえませんか？
lines.english: Kenta, could you teach me how to make that curry?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sou ieba, kenta-kun, shougi ni kyoumi ga aru tte itte imashita yo ne.
lines.ja: そういえば、ケンタくん、将棋に興味があるって言っていましたよね。
lines.kana: そういえば、けんたくん、しょうぎにきょうみがあるっていっていましたよね。
lines.english: Oh, and come to think of it, you said you were interested in shogi, didn't you?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: shougi nara, jishin ga arimasu kara, watashi ga oshiemasu yo.
lines.ja: 将棋なら、自信がありますから、私が教えますよ。
lines.kana: しょうぎなら、じしんがありますから、わたしがおしえますよ。
lines.english: Shogi, on the other hand, I'm confident at, so I'll teach you.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: doyoubi wa dou desu ka? konna ni shuumatsu o tanoshimi ni suru no wa, hisashiburi desu.
lines.ja: 土曜日はどうですか？こんなに週末を楽しみにするのは、久しぶりです。
lines.kana: どようびはどうですか？こんなにしゅうまつをたのしみにするのは、ひさしぶりです。
lines.english: How's Saturday for you? It's been a long time since I looked forward to a weekend this much.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kenta-kun mo, shougi, ki ni itte kureru to ii n desu ga.
lines.ja: ケンタくんも、将棋、気に入ってくれるといいんですが。
lines.kana: けんたくんも、しょうぎ、きにいってくれるといいんですが。
lines.english: I hope you'll take to shogi, too.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: jaa, doyoubi, tanoshimi ni shite imasu. shitsurei shimasu.
lines.ja: じゃあ、土曜日、楽しみにしています。失礼します。
lines.kana: じゃあ、どようび、たのしみにしています。しつれいします。
lines.english: Well then, I'm looking forward to Saturday. Goodbye for now.

questions.english: What does Satou-san want to do?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、何がしたいんですか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、なにがしたいんですか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, nani ga shitai n desu ka?

choices.english: Find out what was in Kenta's curry, because something in it didn't agree with him.
Swap lessons: Kenta teaches him shogi, and he teaches Kenta to make curry.
Learn to make Kenta's curry, and teach Kenta shogi in return, on Saturday.

questions.explanation: Lines 3 and 5: Satou-san loved Kenta's curry (ki ni itte, ki ni itta) and wants to try making it himself. Line 7: he asks Kenta to teach him how (karee no tsukurikata, oshiete moraemasen ka?). Lines 8-9: Kenta once said he was interested in shogi, and Satou-san is confident at shogi, so he'll do the teaching there (watashi ga oshiemasu yo). Line 10: he suggests Saturday, and line 12 closes with doyoubi, tanoshimi ni shite imasu. A is wrong: in line 4 'hitotsu ki ni natta' means one thing made him curious. He asks what was in the curry because he wants to make it (line 5), not because something bothered him. B swaps the roles: Satou-san is the one who isn't confident about cooking (line 6) and who is confident at shogi (line 9).

questions.english: Satou-san says, "hontou ni ki ni itte, kesa mo tabemashita yo." How did he feel about the curry?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、カレーをどう思いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、かれーをどうおもいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, karee o dou omoimashita ka?

choices.english: He felt sure he could make it himself.

questions.explanation: Line 3: ki ni iru is taking a liking to something, and once it has happened Japanese uses the past or -te form, even where English says 'I love it': ki ni itte here, ki ni itta in line 5. He loved it so much he ate it again this morning (kesa mo tabemashita) and wants to make it himself (line 5). B is ki ni naru, which sounds close: in line 4 he does say 'hitotsu ki ni natta n desu ga', but that's 'one thing made me curious' about what was in it, and it's natta, not itta. C is the opposite of line 6, where he says he has no confidence making meals (jishin ga nakute).

questions.english: Satou-san says how he has always felt about cooking. What did he say?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、料理について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、りょうりについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, ryouri ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I've always been confident about cooking
choices.romaji: zutto, ryouri ni jishin ga atta

choices.english: I've always been interested in cooking
choices.romaji: zutto, ryouri ni kyoumi ga atta

choices.english: I've always been 'interest' in cooking (a calque of 'interested')

questions.explanation: Line 6: 'zutto, ryouri ni kyoumi ga atta n desu'. In Japanese the interest exists (kyoumi ga aru, here past atta), and the topic takes ni: ryouri ni. He uses it again in line 8 about Kenta (shougi ni kyoumi ga aru). A swaps in the chunk's contrast partner, jishin: he says the opposite about cooking in the same line (jishin ga nakute, no confidence). C is the English adjective turned into kyoumi + desu, which Japanese doesn't say; you don't 'be' interest, you have it (kyoumi ga aru).

questions.english: Kenta asks you, "doyoubi, uchi de karee tsukuru kedo, kuru?" (I'm making curry at my place on Saturday. Want to come?) Say yes, and that you're looking forward to it.
questions.ja: 土曜日、うちでカレー作るけど、来る？
questions.kana: どようび、うちでかれーつくるけど、くる？
questions.romaji: doyoubi, uchi de karee tsukuru kedo, kuru?
questions.answer: Say you'll come and that you're looking forward to it with tanoshimi ni shiteru, the -te ru form for how you feel now. What you're looking forward to can go first, with o dropped (kenta no karee, tanoshimi ni shiteru).

modelAnswers.romaji: iku iku! tanoshimi ni shiteru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 行く行く！楽しみにしてるね。
modelAnswers.english: I'm in! Looking forward to it.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, iku! kenta no karee, tanoshimi ni shiteru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、行く！ケンタのカレー、楽しみにしてるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'll come! I'm looking forward to your curry.

questions.explanation: Satou-san closes with 'doyoubi, tanoshimi ni shite imasu' (line 12), and in line 10 says 'konna ni shuumatsu o tanoshimi ni suru no wa, hisashiburi desu'. English 'look forward to' has no matching verb: Japanese makes the event a pleasure ahead, tanoshimi ni suru, in the -te ru form for how you feel now (shiteru; polite shite imasu). Don't say matenai for 'I can't wait': it sounds like you've run out of patience. Kenta asks casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: Imagine you're Kenta. On Saturday, Satou-san sets out the shogi board and asks, "kenta-kun, shougi wa tsuyoi desu ka?" (Are you any good at shogi?) You've hardly ever played. Tell him you're not confident.
questions.ja: ケンタくん、将棋は強いですか？
questions.kana: けんたくん、しょうぎはつよいですか？
questions.romaji: kenta-kun, shougi wa tsuyoi desu ka?
questions.answer: Say you're not confident with jishin and nai: jishin nai desu (ga dropped) or jishin ga arimasen. Stay polite: he's your older neighbour.

modelAnswers.romaji: iya, jishin nai desu. oshiete kudasai.
modelAnswers.ja: いや、自信ないです。教えてください。
modelAnswers.english: Oh no, I'm not confident. Please teach me.

modelAnswers.romaji: iie, mada jishin ga arimasen. yoroshiku onegai shimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: いいえ、まだ自信がありません。よろしくお願いします。
modelAnswers.english: No, I'm not confident yet. Please go easy on me.

questions.explanation: Satou-san says 'jishin ga nakute' about cooking (line 6) and 'jishin ga arimasu' about shogi (line 9). English 'confident' is an adjective, but in Japanese confidence is something you have or don't: jishin (ga) aru / nai, with ga often dropped (jishin nai desu). Don't say jishin desu, which sounds like 'It's an earthquake!' (jishin also means earthquake), and a bare wakarimasen just means 'I don't know'. He's an older neighbour, so keep it polite.

newWords.english: how to make something (tsukuru + -kata, way of)
